In [[algebraic geometry]], '''universal algebraic geometry''' generalizes the geometry of [[Ring (mathematics)|rings]] to geometries of arbitrary [[Variety (universal algebra)|varieties of algebras]], so that every variety of algebras has its own algebraic geometry. The two terms ''[[algebraic variety]]'' and ''variety of algebras'' should not be confused.
